extraction_metadata.notes: In-silico screening of flavonoid library against mitochondrial-cascade targets to identify neuroprotective candidates. The mitochondrial cascade hypothesis places apoptosis upstream of Caspase-3 — different mechanism class from Magnoflorine's direct Caspase-3 inhibition.

title: Uncovering potential neuroprotective flavonoids targeting the mitochondrial cascade: an in-silico screening approach
subtitle_or_tagline: A library-scale flavonoid screen against mitochondrial-cascade targets — a different mechanism class from direct Caspase-3 inhibition.
topic: A curated flavonoid library is screened in silico against mitochondrial-cascade targets (mitochondrial permeability transition pore, Bax/Bcl-2 axis, cytochrome c release) to identify candidates that prevent inflammation-induced neuronal cell death upstream of Caspase-3 activation.

components.name: Flavonoid library
components.role: Curated set of natural-product flavonoids with known bioavailability and safety data.

components.name: Target panel
components.role: Mitochondrial-cascade proteins: Bax, Bcl-2, VDAC, cytochrome c, mitochondrial permeability transition pore components.

components.name: Scoring pipeline
components.role: Docking + binding-affinity scoring + ADMET filtering (including BBB prediction).

architecture.data_flow: Flavonoid structures → Docking vs mitochondrial targets → affinity ranking → ADMET / BBB filtering → top candidates for in-vitro validation.

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Assemble the flavonoid library from natural-product databases.
Step 3 - Dock each flavonoid against each target.
Step 4 - Rank by binding affinity; filter by ADMET / BBB.
Step 5 - Select top candidates for in-vitro validation (future work).
Step 6 - Map candidates to mechanism classes (Bax modulation, mPTP blockade, cytochrome c release inhibition).
key_claims: The mitochondrial cascade is a viable upstream intervention point — distinct from direct Caspase-3 inhibition.
Multiple flavonoids showed favorable docking against mitochondrial-cascade targets.
BBB permeability varies widely across the flavonoid family — a key differentiator for CNS repurposing.
Combined docking + ADMET filtering narrows the library to a tractable shortlist for experimental validation.
Mechanism class (upstream mitochondrial) complements rather than competes with direct Caspase-3 inhibition.

effect_sizes.unit: % of library passing combined docking + ADMET filter
effect_sizes.note: Interpretation: ~5% of the flavonoid library passed the combined docking + ADMET filter as a candidate shortlist.

caveats_or_warnings: In-silico screens are hypothesis generators; no cellular validation in this paper.
Mitochondrial-cascade intervention is mechanistically upstream of Caspase-3; effect on final apoptosis rate requires experimental confirmation.
BBB permeability predictions in this paper are rule-based; ML models trained on known CNS drugs would be more accurate.
Flavonoid library coverage is biased toward well-studied subclasses — underexplored scaffolds may be missed.

molecule_metadata.name: Flavonoid library (multiple structures)
molecule_metadata.class: Polyphenolic natural products (flavones, flavanones, flavonols, isoflavones)

molecule_metadata.notable: Library-scale: average MW ~270 Da (planar scaffold) — generally favorable BBB permeability. The BBB predictor should score this family as BBB-penetrant on average, with subclass-specific variation.
molecule_metadata.tradition: Centuries of dietary and TCM use across multiple subclasses.
